In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

﴿All praise is due to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to whom belongs praise in the Hereafter. And He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.﴾.

The surahs that open with praise (al-hamd) are five. Two of them are in the first half of the Qur'an: al-An'am and al-Kahf. Two are in the latter part: this surah and Surat al-Mala'ikah. The fifth is the Opening of the Book (Fatihat al-Kitab), which is recited with the first half and with the latter half. The wisdom in this is that the blessings of Allah, despite their abundance and our inability to count them, are confined to two categories: the blessing of origination (ni'mat al-ijad) and the blessing of continuance (ni'mat al-ibqa'). Allah the Exalted created us first by His mercy and created for us what we need to sustain ourselves. This blessing is found again through restoration (al-i'adah), for He will create us once more and create for us what endures. So for us there are two states, beginning and restoration, and in each state Allah the Exalted bestows upon us two blessings: the blessing of origination and the blessing of continuance.

In the first half He said: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light﴾ [al-An'am: 1], indicating thanks for the blessing of origination. This is shown by His words in the same surah: ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾ [al-An'am: 2], indicating the first origination. In the second surah, which is al-Kahf, He said: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who revealed to His servant the Book and did not make in it any crookedness, [but made it] upright﴾ [al-Kahf: 1–2], indicating thanks for the blessing of continuance, for the sharī'ahs (divine laws) are the means of continuance. Were there no law to which creation submits, each person would follow his own desire, disputes would arise over ambiguous matters, and that would lead to killing and mutual destruction.

Then in this surah He said: ﴿All praise is due to Allah﴾, indicating the second blessing of origination. This is shown by His words: ﴿and to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter﴾. In the surah of the angels He said: ﴿All praise is due to Allah﴾, indicating the blessing of continuance. This is shown by His words: ﴿Who makes the angels messengers﴾ [Fatir: 1]. All the angels will not be messengers except on the Day of Resurrection, when Allah will send them with greetings of peace, as He said: ﴿And the angels will receive them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103], and He said about them: ﴿Peace be upon you; you have done well, so enter it, abiding forever﴾ [al-Zumar: 73]. The Opening of the Book, since it includes mention of both blessings through His words: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatihah: 2], indicating the immediate blessing,

[Page 207]

and His words: ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ [al-Fatihah: 4], indicating the deferred blessing, is recited at the beginning and at the end. Then there are several issues:

First issue: al-hamd is gratitude (shukr), and gratitude is for a blessing. Allah the Exalted made what is in the heavens and the earth belong to Himself by His words: ﴿to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, and He did not state that it belongs to us so that gratitude would be obligatory. Our answer to this is: praise (al-hamd) differs from gratitude (shukr) in one respect, which is that praise is more general. One is praised for having good qualities even if he has not bestowed any favour upon the one praising him at all. It is proper for a person to say about a scholar he has never met: "He is a knowledgeable, active, excellent, and perfect man." It is said of him that he praises so-and-so, and it is not said that he thanks him, unless he mentions his blessings or mentions him in connection with his blessings. Allah the Exalted is praised eternally for His attributes of perfection and His qualities of majesty, and He is thanked, and will always be thanked, for the generosity He has displayed and the blessings He has bestowed. So mention of a blessing is not required for praise; mention of His greatness suffices. In His being the Owner of whatever is in the heavens and the earth is complete greatness, so to Him belongs praise. Moreover, we say: His words ﴿to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ necessitate a more complete gratitude than what His words ﴿He created for you whatever is on the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 29] necessitate, because when whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, and we are the ones who benefit from it and not He, that necessitates a gratitude that is not necessitated by its being ours.

Second issue: You have stated that praise here indicates the blessing that is in the Hereafter, so why did Allah mention the heavens and the earth? We say: the blessings of the Hereafter are not visible, so Allah mentioned the visible blessings, which are what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. Then He said: ﴿and to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter﴾, so that the blessings of the Hereafter may be compared with the blessings of this world and their superiority may be known through their permanence and the perishing of the immediate world. For this reason He said: ﴿And He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware﴾, indicating that the creation of these things is by wisdom and goodness. Wisdom (al-hikmah) is an attribute that is established for Allah and cannot cease, so it is possible for Him to create the like of these again in the Hereafter.

Third issue: Wisdom (al-hikmah) is knowledge to which action is connected. For one who knows a matter and does not act in accordance with his knowledge is not called wise. The agent whose action accords with knowledge is the wise one. The Aware (al-khabir) is one who knows the consequences of affairs and their inner realities. So His words "Wise" mean: at the beginning He creates as is fitting. "Aware" means: in the end He knows what proceeds from the created being and what does not proceed, and to what the destiny of each person will be. So He is wise in the beginning and aware in the end.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 34, verses 2–3:**

Then Allah explained, as He had informed him, by His saying: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends into it. And He is the Merciful, the Forgiving.﴾

"What enters into the earth" is the seed (al-habbah) and the dead; "what comes out of it" is the ears of grain (al-sanabil) and the living. "What descends from the sky" is of the kinds of His mercy, among which are the rain, among which are the angels, and among which is the Qur'an. "What ascends into it" is, among it, the good word, according to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾, and among it are the righteous spirits, and among it are the righteous deeds, according to His saying: ﴿And the righteous deed raises it﴾ [Fatir: 10]. And there are issues (masa'il) in this:

Page 208

The first issue: He placed "what enters into the earth" before "what descends from the sky" because the seed is first sown and then watered afterward.

The second issue: He said "and what ascends into it" and did not say "ascends to it," indicating the acceptance of righteous deeds and the rank of pure souls. This is because the word "ila" (to) denotes a limit (al-ghayah). Had He said "and what ascends to it," it would have been understood as stopping at the heavens. So He said: ﴿and what ascends into it﴾ so that its penetration into them and its ascent from them would be understood. For this reason He said regarding the good word: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾, because Allah is the ultimate end, and there is no rank beyond reaching Him. As for the sky, it is the lower realm, and above it is the ultimate end.

The third issue: He said: ﴿And He is the Merciful, the Forgiving﴾. Merciful in the sending down, in that He sends down provision from the sky; Forgiving when the spirits and deeds ascend to Him. So He showed mercy first by the sending down and forgave second at the ascent.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 34, verse 4:

Then He explained that this blessing by which God deserves praise, which is the blessing of the Hereafter, was denied by a people, so He said, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you, the Knower of the unseen. Not an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth escapes from Him, and not what is smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register."﴾ ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds. Those will have forgiveness and noble provision.﴾

He informed of its coming and confirmed it with an oath. Al-Zamakhshari, may God have mercy on him, said: If someone says: How does emphasis by oath hold, given that they say: "There is no Lord," even though they say it, yet a matter of usul (fundamental doctrine) is not established by oath? He answered this by saying that He did not limit Himself to the oath, but mentioned the evidence, which is His saying: ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾. And the explanation of it being evidence is that the evildoer may remain in this world for a long period in fleeting pleasures and die upon them, and the doer of good may endure in the abode of this world in severe pains for a period and die in them. So if there were no abode in which the recompenses are given, the matter would be contrary to wisdom. But what I say is that the evidence mentioned in His saying: ﴿Knower of the unseen; not an atom's weight escapes from Him﴾ is more evident, because when He is knowing of all things, He knows the parts of living beings and is able to gather them, so the Hour is possible to occur, and the Truthful One has informed of it, so it will be realized. On this basis, His saying, exalted is He: ﴿in the heavens or on the earth﴾ contains a subtle point, which is that a human being has a body and a soul, and bodies have their parts in the earth, and souls are in the heaven. So His saying: ﴿not an atom's weight escapes from Him in the heavens﴾ is an indication of His knowledge of souls, and His saying: ﴿or on the earth﴾ is an indication of His knowledge of bodies. And when He knows souls and forms and is able to gather them, there remains no improbability in the resurrection. And His saying: ﴿nor what is smaller than that or greater﴾ is an indication that the mention of the atom's weight is not for limitation, but that what is smaller than it does not escape Him. On this basis, if someone says: What need is there to mention the greater? For whoever knows the smaller than the atom must know the greater? We say: Since God, exalted is He, intended to explain the establishing of matters in the Book, if He had limited Himself to the smaller, one would suppose that He records only minor things, since they are the locus of forgetfulness, whereas the greater is not forgotten, so there is no need to record it. Therefore He said: The recording in the Book is not so, for the greater is also written in it. Then, when He explained His knowledge of minor and major things, He mentioned that the gathering of all that and its recording is for the recompense, so He said: ﴿That He may reward those who believed and did righteous deeds. Those will have forgiveness and noble provision.﴾ He mentioned two matters concerning them: faith and righteous deeds, and mentioned for them two matters: forgiveness and noble provision. So forgiveness is the recompense of faith, so every believer is forgiven, and this is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, God does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa: 48], and by His saying, peace be upon him, in what Taj al-Din Isa ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hakim al-Bandahi informed us, saying: My father informed me from my grandfather from Muhyi al-Sunnah from Abd al-Wahid al-Maliji from Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi from Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firbri from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari: "Whoever says there is no god but God, and in his heart is the weight of an atom of faith, will come out of the Fire." And the noble provision is from righteous deeds, and this is fitting, for whoever works for a noble master a deed, upon finishing the work he must bestow upon him a favor and feed him food. As for describing the provision as noble, we have mentioned that it means possessing nobility or bestowing honor, or because it comes without being sought, unlike the provision of this world, for it does not come unless one seeks it and takes the means to it. And in the interpretation there are issues:

The first issue: His saying: ﴿Those will have forgiveness and noble provision﴾ admits of two aspects:

One: that this be theirs as a recompense, so He delivers it to them, by His saying: ﴿That He may reward those who believed﴾.

Second: that this be theirs, and God recompenses them with something else, because His saying: ﴿Those will have﴾ is a complete nominal sentence, and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That He may reward those who believed﴾ is an independent verbal sentence, and this is more emphatic in glad tidings than the saying of a speaker: "That He may reward those who believed with provision."

The second issue: The lam in "li-yajziya" is for causation, its meaning being the Hereafter for the recompense. If someone says: What is the aspect of the connection? We say: God, exalted is He, willed that His reward not be cut off, so He made for the accountable person an enduring abode, so that his reward would reach him continually forever, and He made before it an abode in which there are pains and illnesses and in which there is death, so that the accountable person would know the measure of what he will be in the Hereafter when he compares it to what came before, and when he considers it in itself.

The third issue: He distinguished the provision by the description in His saying: "noble," and did not describe the forgiveness, because the provision is one thing for the believers, and from it is the tree of zaqqum and boiling water, and from it are fruits and pure drink, so He distinguished the provision because division occurs in it, and did not distinguish the forgiveness because there is no division in it.

Then God the Exalted said: ﴿And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them, for them is a punishment of a painful torment.﴾

When He had explained the state of the believers on the Day of Resurrection, He explained the state of the disbelievers. His saying ﴿And those who strive against Our signs﴾ means "striving to nullify them," and its meaning is: those who denied Our signs. In this case it stands in contrast to what preceded, because His saying ﴿believe﴾ means "affirm," and this means "deny." If it is asked, "How is it known that their striving is for nullification, when what is mentioned is unqualified striving?" We reply: it is understood from His saying ﴿seeking to frustrate them﴾. This is because it is a circumstantial clause whose meaning is "they strove against them while intending to frustrate them." Striving in establishing and conveying does not make the striver one who frustrates, because the Qur'an and the signs of God are miraculous in themselves and need no one. As for the denier, he comes with the concealment of clear signs, so he needs great striving and intense effort to promote his lie, perhaps to frustrate the one who holds fast to the truth. It has also been said that what is meant by His saying ﴿seeking to frustrate them﴾ is "thinking that they can escape God," and on this view the striver's being a striver in falsehood is in the utmost clarity. ﴿For them is a punishment﴾ stands in contrast to ﴿For them is a provision﴾.

There are several subtleties in the verse.

The first: Here He said ﴿For them is a punishment﴾ and did not say "God will recompense them." We have already stated earlier that His saying ﴿that He may recompense those who believed﴾ allows that God recompenses them with something else. His saying ﴿those, for them is forgiveness﴾ is a report about their deserved due prepared for them. In sum, the possibility of an addition there stands, in view of His saying ﴿that He may recompense﴾, whereas here He did not say "that He may requite them," so that possibility does not arise here.

The second: There He said "for them is forgiveness," then He added to it, saying ﴿and a generous provision﴾. Here He said only ﴿for them is a punishment of a painful torment﴾. The answer has already been given regarding its like.

The third: There He said ﴿for them is forgiveness and a generous provision﴾ and did not qualify it with the partitive "min," so He did not say "for them is a portion of provision," nor "a provision of a noble kind." Here He said ﴿for them is a punishment of a painful torment﴾ with a word suitable for partition. All of this indicates the vastness of mercy and the scarcity of wrath in comparison to it. It is said that ar-rijz is the worst of punishments, and on this view "min" is for specifying the kind, like the speaker's saying "a ring of silver."

Regarding the word ﴿alim﴾ (painful) there are two readings: the genitive (al-jarr) and the nominative (ar-raf'). The nominative is on the basis that ﴿alim﴾ is an attribute of ﴿adhab﴾ (punishment), as if He had said "a painful punishment of the worst punishment." The genitive is on the basis that it is an attribute of ﴿rijz﴾. The nominative is closer in view of the meaning, and the genitive in view of the wording.

If it is asked: why are the categories restricted to the righteous believer whose deeds are good and the denier who strives and frustrates? It is possible that someone is a believer with no good deed, or a disbeliever whose state is undetermined. We reply: when the states of the two mentioned groups are known, it is known that the believer is close in rank to those whose matter was mentioned earlier, and the disbeliever is close in rank to those whose mention preceded. For the believer there is forgiveness and a generous provision, even if he is not equal in honor to the provision of one who did righteous deeds; and for the non-obstinate disbeliever there is punishment, even if it is not among the worst kinds reserved for obstinate deniers.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.﴾

When He had explained the condition of the one who strives to deny [the message] in the Hereafter, He explained his condition in this world, namely that his striving is futile. For whoever has been given knowledge is not deceived by the denial [of others], and he knows that what was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ) is true and sincere. His saying, "it is the truth" (huwa al-ḥaqq), conveys restriction (al-ḥaṣr, exclusive limitation), meaning that the truth is nothing other than that. As for the statement of the denier, it is false. This is unlike when two adversaries dispute, where the dispute is verbal, so that each party's statement is true in meaning.

As for His saying, ﴿and it guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, it may be an explanation of its being "the truth," since it guides to this path. It may also be an explanation of another benefit: that, along with being true and guiding, the truth is deserving of acceptance, so how much more so when it has a benefit for the future, namely arriving at God.

His saying, ﴿the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, conveys both desire and dread. For when He is Mighty, He is one who exacts retribution, and He will take vengeance upon the one who strives to deny [the message]. And when He is Praiseworthy, He thanks the effort of the one who believes and does righteous deeds.

If it is said: How does He place the attribute that evokes awe before the attribute that evokes mercy, when you always strive to show the precedence of the aspect of mercy? We say: His being Mighty, of complete awe and severe retribution, strengthens the aspect of desire, because the pleasure of the Mighty, the Compeller, is more honorable and nobler than the pleasure of one who is not like that. Thus might, just as it frightens, also gives hope, and just as it discourages from denial, it encourages affirmation, so that nearness to the Mighty may be attained.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Has he invented a lie against God, or is there madness in him?﴾ No, rather those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment and in far-off error. This verse allows two interpretations:

The first: it is the continuation of the speech of those who disbelieved earlier, namely the words of the one who said, ﴿Shall we direct you to a man?﴾

The second: it is the words of a listener who answers the one who said, ﴿Shall we direct you to a man?﴾ It is as if the listener, when he heard the speaker say, ﴿Shall we direct you to a man?﴾, said to him: "Does he invent a lie against God, if he believes otherwise? Or is there in him a *jinnah* [i.e., *junun*], madness, if he does not believe otherwise?" (And in this there is a subtle point.) The subtle point is that the disbeliever does not want his lie to be shown to be a lie. For this reason he divided the matter and did not assert definitively that he was a fabricator, but said "a fabricator or a madman," to avoid someone saying: "How can he say he is a fabricator, when it is possible that he thinks the truth is that? The thought of truthfulness prevents calling the speaker a fabricator and a liar in some situations. Do you not see that one who says, 'Zayd has come,' and then it becomes clear that he did not come, and it is said to him, 'You lied,' he says, 'I did not lie; I only heard from so-and-so that he had come, so I thought he was truthful'? He thus repels the charge of lying from himself by means of supposition." So they guarded against their lie becoming evident. Every intelligent person should therefore guard against his lie becoming evident among people, and an intelligent person should not be lower in rank than the disbeliever.

Then God answered them a second time and said: ﴿No, rather those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment﴾, corresponding to their words, ﴿Has he invented a lie against God?﴾, and His words, ﴿and far-off error﴾, corresponding to their words, ﴿or is there madness in him?﴾ Both are appropriate.

As for the punishment: attributing a lie to a truthful person is harmful, because it is a testimony against him that he deserves punishment. So punishment was placed upon them, since they attributed the lie to him.

As for madness: attributing madness to a sane person is less harmful, because it does not testify against him that he will be punished; rather, it attributes to him a lack of guidance. So He made clear that they are the ones who are astray. Then He described their error as "far-off," because whoever calls the guided one astray is himself the one astray, and whoever calls the one who guides astray is even more astray.

We have mentioned repeatedly that whoever works a task for a king, and knows that he is in the king's sight, performs the work well, perfects it, and strives in it. He mentioned what he gained through repentance, saying: ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind; its morning course was a month's journey and its evening course a month's journey. And We caused a font of copper to flow for him. And among the jinn were those who worked before him by the permission of his Lord. And whoever of them deviates from Our command, We will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze.﴾ On this there are several issues:

The first issue: "And to Solomon the wind" has been read in the nominative and in the accusative. The reading in the nominative: "And to Solomon the wind [is] subjected," or "was subjected to Solomon the wind." The reading in the accusative: "And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind." The nominative has another aspect, which is that it is said: its meaning is "and to Solomon the wind," as one says "to Zayd the house," because the wind was for him like a owned slave specific to him, who commands it with whatever he wants, wherever he wants.

The second issue: The conjunction "wa" is for coordination. On the reading in the nominative, this becomes coordination of a nominal sentence upon a verbal sentence, which is not permissible or not good. How is this? We say: when He explained the state of Dawud, it is as if He, exalted is He, said: what we mentioned was for Dawud, and to Solomon the wind. As for the accusative, according to our saying: ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾, it is as if He said: "And We made iron soft for Dawud, and We subjected the wind for Solomon."

The third issue: The one subjected to Solomon was a specific wind, not these winds, for these are generally beneficial at times of need. What indicates this is that it was read only in the singular, and no one read "al-riyah" (the winds).

And from the subjection of the wind: he tamed horses, which are like the wind. His saying ﴿its morning course was a month's journey﴾ means thirty farsakh, because one who goes out for pleasure usually does not travel more than one farsakh and returns the same. His saying about Dawud: ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ and His saying about Solomon: ﴿And We caused a font of copper to flow for him﴾ [means] that they extracted the melting of iron and copper by fire and used tools made of them, and "the devils" means strong men. All of this is false; what led him to this is weakness of his belief and his not relying on the power of God, while God is capable of every possibility, and these are possible things.

The fifth issue: I say: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We subjected the mountains with Dawud﴾ [al-Anbiya: 79] and His saying: ﴿And to Solomon the wind, violent﴾. If someone asked: what is the wisdom in God, exalted is He, saying in the prophets: ﴿And We subjected the mountains with Dawud﴾, while in this surah He said: ﴿O mountains, echo along with him﴾, and said about the wind there and here: ﴿to Solomon﴾? We say: the mountains, when they glorified, were honored by the mention of God, so He did not attribute them to Dawud with the preposition of possession, but made them with him as a companion. The wind was not mentioned as glorifying, so He made it like a possession of his. This is good. There is another intelligible matter that appears to me: that on our saying ﴿echo with him﴾, meaning "travel," the mountain in traveling is not the principal; rather it moves with him by following. The wind does not move with Solomon; rather it moves Solomon with itself. So He did not say "the wind with Solomon," but Solomon was with the wind. ﴿And We caused a font of copper to flow for him﴾, that is, copper. ﴿And among the jinn﴾, that is, We subjected to him from the jinn. This indicates that all of them were not under his command, and this is the apparent meaning.

Know that God, exalted is He, mentioned three things concerning Dawud and three concerning Solomon, upon both of them be prayer and peace. The mountains subjected to Dawud are of the same kind as the subjection of the wind to Solomon, because the heavy together with what is lighter than it, when they move, the light overtakes the heavy and the heavy remains in its place. But the mountains were heavier than the human, and the human is heavier than the wind. So God decreed that the heavy travel with the light, that is, the mountains with Dawud, as we said: ﴿Echo﴾, that is, travel; and Solomon and his hosts with the wind, the heavy with the light also. The birds are of the same kind as the subjection of the jinn, because these two do not gather with humans: the bird flees from humans, and humans flee from the jinn, for a human avoids the places of the jinn, and the jinn always seeks to hunt humans, and humans seek to hunt birds. So God decreed that the bird would not flee from Dawud but would be tame with him and seek him, and Solomon does not flee from the jinn but subjugates and employs them. As for the copper and the iron, their attraction to each other is not hidden. (Here is a subtle point): that the human should guard against the jinn and avoid them, and association with them leads to corruption. That is why God, exalted is He, said: ﴿I seek refuge in You from the whisperings of the devils﴾ and ﴿I seek refuge in You, my Lord, from their presence﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 97–98]. This is because "Lord" (Rabb) is a term that indicates mercy. So when the reference was to the preservation of Solomon, peace be upon him, He said: ﴿his Lord﴾, and when the reference was to their punishment, He said: ﴿Our command﴾, with the term of magnification that necessitates increased fear. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze﴾ has two aspects:

The first: that the angels were appointed over them and in their hands were rods of fire, so the reference is to that.

The second: that the Blaze is what will be in the Hereafter, so He threatened them with the punishment of the Hereafter.

It has been said: the "an" (أنْ) here is explanatory (tafsiriyyah), meaning "i.e." (أيْ): "Make coats of mail." This is the explanation of ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾, and its realization is that he would work [it]; that is, "We made iron soft for him so that he would make coats of mail." It is also possible to say: "We inspired him that make," and "an" with the imperfect verb gives the verbal noun, so the meaning is: "We made iron soft for him and inspired him to the work of coats of mail (sabighat), which are the wide coats of mail." He mentioned the attribute and the qualified noun is understood from it.

﴿And measure well in the links (al-sard)﴾. The exegetes said: that is, do not make the nails too thick so that the hole becomes wide, and do not widen the hole so that the nails become loose in it. It is also possible to say that al-sard is the work of making the mail (al-zard), and His saying ﴿measure well in al-sard﴾, that is, al-zard, is an indication that he was not commanded with an obligatory command; rather it is earning a living (iktisab), and earning should be according to need. The rest of the days and nights are for worship. So measure in that work, and do not occupy all your times with earning; rather, obtain by it only sustenance and nothing more. This is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do righteous deeds﴾, that is, you were created only for righteous deeds, so do them and increase in them, and in earning, be measured. Then He emphasized the demand for righteous action by His saying: ﴿Indeed I am Seeing of what you do.﴾

We have mentioned repeatedly that whoever works a task for a king, and knows that he is in the king's sight, performs the work well, perfects it, and strives in it. Then, when He mentioned the one penitent, He mentioned another penitent, who is Solomon, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body, then he turned back in repentance﴾ [Sad: 34].

He mentioned what he gained through repentance, saying: ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind; its morning course was a month's journey and its evening course a month's journey. And We caused a font of copper to flow for him. And among the jinn were those who worked before him by the permission of his Lord. And whoever of them deviates from Our command, We will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze.﴾ On this there are several issues:

The first issue: "And to Solomon the wind" has been read in the nominative and in the accusative. The reading in the nominative: "And to Solomon the wind [is] subjected," or "was subjected to Solomon the wind." The reading in the accusative: "And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind." The nominative has another aspect, which is that it is said: its meaning is "and to Solomon the wind," as one says "to Zayd the house," because the wind was for him like a owned slave specific to him, who commands it with whatever he wants, wherever he wants.

The second issue: The conjunction "wa" is for coordination. On the reading in the nominative, this becomes coordination of a nominal sentence upon a verbal sentence, which is not permissible or not good. How is this? We say: when He explained the state of Dawud, it is as if He, exalted is He, said: what we mentioned was for Dawud, and to Solomon the wind. As for the accusative, according to our saying: ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾, it is as if He said: "And We made iron soft for Dawud, and We subjected the wind for Solomon."

The third issue: The one subjected to Solomon was a specific wind, not these winds, for these are generally beneficial at times of need. What indicates this is that it was read only in the singular, and no one read "al-riyah" (the winds).

The fourth issue: Some people said: what is meant by the subjection of the mountains and their glorifying along with Dawud is that they used to glorify as everything glorifies, ﴿And there is not a thing but it glorifies His praise﴾ [al-Isra: 44], and he, peace be upon him, would understand their glorification and glorify. And from the subjection of the wind: he tamed horses, which are like the wind. His saying ﴿its morning course was a month's journey﴾ means thirty farsakh, because one who goes out for pleasure usually does not travel more than one farsakh and returns the same. His saying about Dawud: ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ and His saying about Solomon: ﴿And We caused a font of copper to flow for him﴾ [means] that they extracted the melting of iron and copper by fire and used tools made of them, and "the devils" means strong men. All of this is false; what led him to this is weakness of his belief and his not relying on the power of God, while God is capable of every possibility, and these are possible things.

The fifth issue: I say: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We subjected the mountains with Dawud﴾ [al-Anbiya: 79] and His saying: ﴿And to Solomon the wind, violent﴾. If someone asked: what is the wisdom in God, exalted is He, saying in the prophets: ﴿And We subjected the mountains with Dawud﴾, while in this surah He said: ﴿O mountains, echo along with him﴾, and said about the wind there and here: ﴿to Solomon﴾? We say: the mountains, when they glorified, were honored by the mention of God, so He did not attribute them to Dawud with the preposition of possession, but made them with him as a companion. The wind was not mentioned as glorifying, so He made it like a possession of his. This is good. There is another intelligible matter that appears to me: that on our saying ﴿echo with him﴾, meaning "travel," the mountain in traveling is not the principal; rather it moves with him by following. The wind does not move with Solomon; rather it moves Solomon with itself. So He did not say "the wind with Solomon," but Solomon was with the wind. ﴿And We caused a font of copper to flow for him﴾, that is, copper. ﴿And among the jinn﴾, that is, We subjected to him from the jinn. This indicates that all of them were not under his command, and this is the apparent meaning.

Know that God, exalted is He, mentioned three things concerning Dawud and three concerning Solomon, upon both of them be prayer and peace. The mountains subjected to Dawud are of the same kind as the subjection of the wind to Solomon, because the heavy together with what is lighter than it, when they move, the light overtakes the heavy and the heavy remains in its place. But the mountains were heavier than the human, and the human is heavier than the wind. So God decreed that the heavy travel with the light, that is, the mountains with Dawud, as we said: ﴿Echo﴾, that is, travel; and Solomon and his hosts with the wind, the heavy with the light also. The birds are of the same kind as the subjection of the jinn, because these two do not gather with humans: the bird flees from humans, and humans flee from the jinn, for a human avoids the places of the jinn, and the jinn always seeks to hunt humans, and humans seek to hunt birds. So God decreed that the bird would not flee from Dawud but would be tame with him and seek him, and Solomon does not flee from the jinn but subjugates and employs them. As for the copper and the iron, their attraction to each other is not hidden. (Here is a subtle point): that the human should guard against the jinn and avoid them, and association with them leads to corruption. That is why God, exalted is He, said: ﴿I seek refuge in You from the whisperings of the devils﴾ and ﴿I seek refuge in You, my Lord, from their presence﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 97–98]. How then did Solomon seek association with them? We say: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿who work before him by the permission of his Lord﴾ is an indication that that presence contained no corruption. (Another subtle point): God, exalted is He, said here: ﴿by the permission of his Lord﴾, using the word "Lord," and said: ﴿And whoever of them deviates from Our command﴾, and did not say "from the command of his Lord." This is because "Lord" (Rabb) is a term that indicates mercy. So when the reference was to the preservation of Solomon, peace be upon him, He said: ﴿his Lord﴾, and when the reference was to their punishment, He said: ﴿Our command﴾, with the term of magnification that necessitates increased fear. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze﴾ has two aspects:

The first: that the angels were appointed over them and in their hands were rods of fire, so the reference is to that.

The second: that the Blaze is what will be in the Hereafter, so He threatened them with the punishment of the Hereafter.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿They make for him whatever he wills of sanctuaries, statues, bowls like water-troughs, and cooking-pots fixed in place. Work, O family of Dawud, in thankfulness; and few of My servants are truly grateful.﴾

"Sanctuaries" (maharib) refers to lofty buildings, and for this reason God said: ﴿when they scaled the sanctuary wall﴾ [Sad 38:21]. "Statues" (tamathil) refers to what is in them of carvings. Then, having mentioned the building, which is the dwelling, he explained what is in the dwelling of the vessels for eating, so he said: ﴿and bowls like water-troughs﴾. The word "jifan" is the plural of "jabiyah," which is the large basin that gathers (yajbi) water, i.e., collects it. It was said that a thousand people would gather around a single bowl. ﴿And cooking-pots fixed in place﴾, i.e., steadfast and not movable because of their size; rather, food was ladled from them into those bowls. There are several issues concerning this:

The first issue: he placed the sanctuaries before the statues because carvings are on buildings. And he mentioned the "bowls" before the "cooking-pots," although cooking-pots are the implements of cooking and bowls are the implements of eating, and cooking comes before eating. We say: when he described the royal buildings, he wished to explain the greatness of the banquet spread in those abodes, and he pointed to the bowls because they are present in it; as for the cooking-pots, they are not present in it and are not brought there. For this reason he said: ﴿fixed in place﴾, i.e., not movable. Then, when he described the state of the great bowls, it would occur to the mind: with what is the food in them cooked? So he pointed to the cooking-pots suited to the bowls.

The second issue: he mentioned, regarding Dawud, his occupation with the instruments of war, and regarding Sulayman, his state of peace, which is dwellings and food. That is because Sulayman was the son of Dawud, and Dawud killed Jalut and the tyrannical kings, and Dawud became established in kingship. So Sulayman was like the son of a king whose father had already secured the kingdom for his son and gathered wealth for him, so he distributes it among his soldiers. Also, because no one could prevail against Sulayman in his estimation, they abandoned war with him; and if anyone fought against him, the time of the war would be brief, since he overtook them by the wind. Thus in his time greatness lay in feeding and bestowing favors.

The third issue: when he said, after God's words ﴿Make full coats of mail﴾ [Saba 34:11], "Work righteousness," he said, after mentioning what the jinn do: ﴿Work, O family of Dawud, in thankfulness﴾, indicating what we mentioned, that these things are of a transitory nature, and a person should not make himself wholly absorbed in them; rather, the obligation that one should increase in is righteous deed that constitutes thankfulness. There is also in this an indication of not being preoccupied with these things and of little concern with them, as in His words: ﴿and measure well in the weaving﴾, i.e., make it in proportion to need.

The fourth issue: the accusative case of "shukran" admits three aspects:

The first: that it is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), like the saying of one who says: "I came to you out of desire, and I worshipped God out of hope for His forgiveness."

The second: that it is a verbal noun (masdar), like the saying of one who says: "I thanked God with thanks," and the verbal noun is from a root other than the verb, like the saying of one who says: "I sat sitting." That is because work is thankfulness, so His words ﴿Work﴾ stand in the place of His words "Give thanks."

The third: that it is an object (maf'ul bihi), like your saying: "Strike Zayd," as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, because thanks is something good.

The fifth issue: His words ﴿and few of My servants are truly grateful﴾ indicate that God lightened the matter for His servants. That is because when He said ﴿Work, O family of Dawud, in thankfulness﴾, it was understood from it that thanks is obligatory, but thanking Him for His favors as is fitting is not possible; for thanks is by means of divine enabling, which is itself a favor requiring another thanks, which is by another enabling. So God's favor after thanks always remains without thanks. Thus God, exalted is He, said: If you are not able to give full thanks, then there is no fault upon you in that, for few of My servants are truly grateful. And what strengthens our view is that He included everyone in His words "My servants," with the attribution to Himself; and "My servants" with the attribution to the speaker's own self has not come in the Qur'an except regarding those who are saved, as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of God's mercy﴾ [az-Zumar 39:53], and His words: ﴿Indeed My servants, you have no authority over them﴾ [al-Hijr 15:42]. If it is said: according to what you have mentioned, full thanks to God is not possible, yet His words ﴿and few﴾ indicate that among His servants there is one who is thankful for His favors. We say: thanks in proportion to human capacity is what actually occurs, and few are those who do it; as for thanks that befits God's favors, there is no ability for it, and God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. Or we say: the one who gives complete thanks is none other than the one with whom God is pleased, and He says to him: "O My servant, what you have brought of little thanks, I have accepted from you, and I have recorded for you that you are thankful for My favors in their entirety." And this acceptance is a great favor, whose thanks I do not burden you with.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And when We decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff. So when he fell, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.﴾

When He had explained the greatness of Sulayman and the subjugation of the wind and the spirits to him, He explained that he did not escape death, and that He decreed death upon him. This is a reminder to creation that death is inevitable. Even if anyone had escaped it, Sulayman would have been the most deserving of escape from it. In this are several issues:

The first issue: Sulayman, peace be upon him, would stand in worship of God for a complete night and a whole day, and at some times longer. He had a staff on which he leaned while standing before his Lord. Then at one point he was standing in his customary worship when he died. His soldiers thought he was still in worship, and he remained in that state for days and continued for months. Then God willed to make the matter manifest to them, so He decreed that a creature of the earth should eat his staff, and he fell and his condition became known.

As for His saying: ﴿So when he fell, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment﴾, the jinn knew what humans do not know, so a person supposed that this degree of knowledge was knowledge of the unseen, but it is not so. Rather, humans have been given only a little knowledge, so most present things are unknown to them, while the jinn knew only apparent things, even though they are hidden relative to humans. The matter became clear to them, that they do not know the unseen, for if they had known it, they would not have remained in the arduous labors, supposing that Sulayman was alive.

His saying: ﴿they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment﴾ is evidence that the believing jinn were not under subjugation, because a believer in the time of the Prophet would not be in the humiliating punishment.

[Page 217]

Then God Most High said: ﴿Certainly there was for Sheba, in their dwelling-place, a sign: two gardens, on the right and on the left. "Eat of the provision of your Lord and give thanks to Him. A good land and a Forgiving Lord."﴾

When God mentioned the state of those who give thanks for His blessings by mentioning Dawud and Sulayman, He then explained the state of those who disbelieve in His blessings, by relating the account of the people of Saba'. Regarding "Saba'" there are two readings: with a fatha, taking it as the name of a place, and with a kasra and tanwin, taking it as the name of a tribe. The latter is the more apparent (al-azhar), because God made the sign to be for Saba', and what understands is the rational being, not the place; so there is no need to supply the word "people" (ahl). His saying ﴿a sign﴾ means "from the bounty of their Lord." Then He explained it by mentioning what it is in apposition to it, in His saying ﴿two gardens, on the right and on the left﴾.

Al-Zamakhshari said: "What sign is there in two gardens, when some regions of Iraq contain thousands of gardens?" He answered that the meaning is that each of them had two gardens, or that on the right and left of their city there were two groups of gardens, and because some of them were joined to others, He made them one garden.

His saying ﴿Eat of the provision of your Lord﴾ indicates the completion of the blessings upon them, since neither fear nor sickness prevented them from eating its fruits. His saying ﴿and give thanks to Him﴾ is also a statement of the perfection of the blessing, for thanks is only required for a blessing that is worthy of regard. Then, having described their condition in their dwellings, their gardens and their eating, He completed the description of the blessing by explaining that there was no harm in it and no consequence in the outcome in this world. So He said: ﴿A good land﴾, meaning pure from harmful things, with no snake, no scorpion, no plague, and no *wakham* (a disease caused by damp, unhealthy air). And He said: ﴿and a Forgiving Lord﴾, meaning there is no punishment for it and no torment in the Hereafter. Hence at this point the perfection of the blessing became clear, since it was a present pleasure free from harmful consequences in the future.

Then, once He had explained what came from His side, He mentioned what came from theirs, saying: ﴿But they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of the Arim, and We replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk, and a few lote-trees.﴾ ﴿That is how We requited them for their disbelief. And do We requite any but the ungrateful?﴾

He thereby showed the extent of their wrongdoing in turning away after the sign had been made clear, as He said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord and then turns away from them?﴾ [al-Sajdah: 22]. Then He explained the manner of the retribution against them, as He said: ﴿Indeed, We will take retribution against the criminals﴾ [al-Sajdah: 22]. Its manner was that God sent upon them a torrent which drowned their wealth and destroyed their dwellings. Regarding "al-Arim" there are several interpretations:

The first: it is the rat (al-Juradh) which caused the ruin of the dam (al-Sikr). This is because Bilqis had built between two mountains with valleys, and she blocked the valleys so that the waters of the rains and springs would gather in them and become like a sea. She made for it three gates arranged one above another, and the gates were opened one after another. The rat then gnawed through the dam, the dam was ruined because of it, and the sea overturned upon them.

The second: al-Arim is the name of the dam (al-Sikr), and it is the plural of al-Arimah, which means stones.

The third: it is the name of the valley from which the water came out. His saying: ﴿and We replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit﴾ shows the permanence of the ruin, because gardens in which people live bear good fruit through cultivation; but when they are left for years they become like a thicket and a jungle, with trees intertwining and harmful plants growing in them, so the fruit becomes scarce and the trees multiply. Al-Khamt is every tree that has thorns, or every tree whose fruit is bitter, or every tree whose fruit cannot be eaten. Al-Athl is a type of tamarisk, and it bears no fruit except at certain times; it has something like galls or something smaller than that in its taste and nature. Al-Sidr is well known, and He said of it "a few" because it was the best of their trees, so God reduced it. Then God explained that this was a requital for their ingratitude, saying: ﴿That is how We requited them for their disbelief. And do We requite any but the ungrateful?﴾, meaning: We do not requite with that recompense ﴿any but the ungrateful﴾. Some scholars said: "mujazah" (requital) is used for punishment, while "jaza'" (recompense) is used for blessing. But His saying ﴿That is how We requited them﴾ indicates that "jaza'" is used for punishment. Perhaps whoever said that derived it from the fact that "mujazah" is a form of reciprocity (mufa'alah), which in most cases occurs between two parties, each taking a recompense on the other's right. In the case of blessing it is not called mujazah, because God the Exalted initiates the blessings.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed visible towns, and We measured out the travel between them: "Travel between them by night and day in security."﴾ ﴿But they said, "Our Lord, make the distances between our journeys farther," and they wronged themselves. So We made them into tales, and We scattered them completely. Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.﴾

"Between them and the towns" means between them and al-Sham, for it is the blessed land. "Visible towns" means that some of them are visible to one another: the dark mass of one village can be seen from another village. If someone says: this is among the blessings, and God has already begun to explain the change of their blessings in His words, ﴿And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens﴾, so how does He return once more to describing the blessing after the curse? We answer: He mentioned the condition of their own land and explained its change into bitter fruit and tamarisk; then He mentioned the condition of the area outside their land and described its prosperity through the abundance of towns; then He mentioned its change into deserts, wastelands and open plains by His words, ﴿Our Lord, make the distances between our journeys farther﴾, and this He did. This is indicated by the reading of those who read (Rabbuna ba'ada) in the form of subject and predicate. As for His words, ﴿and We measured out the travel in them﴾: inhabited places have known and measured stations that are not exceeded. Since between every two towns there was a distance of half a day's travel, and they would set out in the morning for one town and return in the evening to another, as far as custom allowed one to go beyond it, that is what is meant by the measuring. But in deserts the travel cannot be measured; rather, the traveler journeys in them according to his strength, diligently, until he crosses them.

His words, ﴿Travel between them by night and day﴾, mean that there were known nights and days between them. His words, ﴿in security﴾, indicate the abundance of settlement, for fear of highway robbers and of being cut off from travelling companions does not arise in such places. It has also been said that the meaning of His words, ﴿by night and day﴾, is: you travel in it, if you wish, by night, and if you wish, by day, because there is no fear, unlike dangerous places, some of which are traversed at night so that the enemy does not learn of their journey, and some of which are traversed by day so that the enemy does not target them, when the enemy is not openly hostile and aggressive.

His words, may He be exalted, ﴿But they said, "Our Lord, make the distances between our journeys farther"﴾: it has been said that they asked for this, and it may bear two meanings. First: they asked out of insolence, as the Jews asked for garlic and onions. Second: it may be due to the corruption of their belief and their firm reliance on the idea that this cannot be done, just as one person says to another, "Strike me," indicating that he cannot do it. It is also possible to say: ﴿they said, "Our Lord, make [them] farther"﴾ by the tongue of their state, meaning: since they disbelieved, they asked that the distances between their journeys be made farther and that the inhabited places of their lands be ruined. His words, ﴿and they wronged themselves﴾, serve as an explanation of this. His words, ﴿So We made them into tales﴾, mean: We dealt with them in a way by which We made them an example, as it is said, "They scattered like the hands of Saba'." His words, ﴿and We scattered them completely﴾, are an explanation of their being made into tales. His words, may He be exalted, ﴿Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful﴾, mean: in what We have mentioned about the condition of the grateful and the ruin of the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 34, verses 22–23:

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claimed besides God. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they have any share in them, nor is there any helper of His among them.﴾ ﴿And intercession with Him does not benefit, except for one whom He permits. Until, when terror is removed from their hearts, they say: "What has your Lord said?" They say: "The truth. And He is the Most High, the Greatest."﴾

When God, exalted is He, had explained the condition of the grateful and the condition of the disbelievers, and had reminded them of those who passed before, He returned to addressing them and said to His Messenger (ﷺ): "Say to the polytheists: Call upon those you claimed besides God, so that they may remove the harm from you," in a mocking manner. Then He explained that they possess nothing, by His saying: ﴿They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth﴾.

Know that the doctrines that lead to polytheism (shirk) are four:

The first is the view of one who says: God, exalted is He, created the sky and the celestial things, and made the earth and earthly things subordinate to them. We are among the earthly things, so we worship the stars and the angels that are in the sky. They are our gods, and God is their God. So God said, in refuting their claim: They do not possess anything in the heavens, as you have acknowledged. And He said: "Nor on the earth," contrary to what you claim.

The second is the view of one who says: The heavens are from God in an absolute sense, while the earthly things are from Him but through the intermediary of the stars. God created the elements and the compounds within them through conjunctions, movements, and risings (of stars). Thus they assigned a share of partnership to other than God in the earth. The earlier ones assigned the earth to other than Him and the sky to Him. So He said, in refuting their view: ﴿Nor do they have any share in them﴾, meaning the earth is like the sky, belonging to God and not to another, and no one else has a portion in it.

The third is the view of one who says: All compounds and events are from God, exalted is He, but He delegated that to the stars. The act of one who is permitted is attributed to the one who permits and is denied to the one permitted. An example: if a king says to his slave, "Strike so-and-so," and he strikes him, it is said by custom, "The king struck him," and it is also correct by custom for someone to say, "So-and-so did not strike him; rather, the king ordered him to be struck, and he was struck." These people made the celestial things specific agents for God. So God said, in refuting their view: ﴿Nor is there any helper of His among them﴾, meaning He did not delegate anything to anything. Rather, He is over all things a Guardian and an Observer.

The fourth is the view of one who says: We worship the idols which are images of the angels, so that they may intercede for us. So God said, in refuting their view: "﴿And intercession with Him does not benefit, except for one whom He permits﴾." Therefore there is no benefit in your worship of other than God, for God does not permit intercession for one who worships other than Him. So by your seeking intercession, you forfeit intercession for yourselves.

His saying: ﴿Until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾ means that the fear is removed from them. It is said: "The camel was de-ticked (qurrida)," when the ticks were removed from it. This is called "intensifying the removal" (tashdid al-salb). Regarding God's saying: ﴿Until, when terror is removed from their hearts, they say: "What has your Lord said?" They say: "The truth"﴾, there are several interpretations:

The first: The terror that occurs at the time of revelation. When God reveals, those in the heavens are struck with terror. Then God removes the terror from them, and they say to Gabriel, peace be upon him: "What did God say?" He says: "He said the truth," meaning the revelation.

The second: The terror concerning the Hour. When God revealed to Muhammad, peace be upon him, ﴿and those in the heavens were struck with terror﴾ [an-Naml: 87], concerning the Resurrection, because the sending of Muhammad, peace be upon him, is one of the signs of the Hour. When that terror was removed from them, they said: "What did God say?" Gabriel said: "The truth," meaning the revelation.

The third: God removes the terror from the hearts at the time of death, so every person acknowledges that what God, exalted is He, said is the truth. That acknowledgment benefits the one whose previous (conduct) was in agreement with it. Then He takes his soul upon the faith that is agreed upon between him and God, exalted is He. That acknowledgment harms the one whose previous conduct was contrary to it, and He takes his soul upon the disbelief that is agreed upon between him and God, exalted is He.

Now that you know this, we say: According to the first two views, His saying ﴿until﴾ is a limit connected to His saying ﴿Say﴾, because He explained it through revelation. The statement of one who says, "Say to so-and-so," is for warning, until the addressee hears what he says. Then, after this speech, he says what must be said. So when He said ﴿Say﴾, those in the heavens were struck with terror, and then the terror was removed from them. According to the third view, it is connected to His saying ﴿you claimed﴾, meaning: you claimed disbelief up to the limit of terror; then you abandoned what you claimed and said, "He said the truth."

According to the first two views, the subject of His saying ﴿they say﴾ is the angels asking Gabriel. According to the third view, it is the disbelievers asking the angels. The subject of His saying ﴿the truth﴾ is, according to the first two views, the angels, and according to the third view, the polytheists.

Know that the Truth (al-Haqq) is that which exists. Since God, exalted is He, His existence is not subject to non-existence, He is the Truth in an absolute sense, which is not overturned by falsehood, which is non-existence. A speech that is true is called "truth," because speech has a connection in external reality through its being connected to what is in the mind, and what is in the mind is connected to what is external. So when one says, "Zayd has come," this utterance is connected to what is in the speaker's mind, and the speaker's mind is connected to what is external. But truthfulness has a connection that exists in external reality, so it acquires a lasting existence. Falsehood has a connection that does not exist in external reality. In that case, either it has no connection in the mind, and it is like the non-existent from the outset, and this is the utterances issuing from a stubborn liar. Or it has a connection in the mind that contradicts what is external, and it is then a false belief, ignorance, or conjecture. But since its object has no reality to connect to, that speech vanishes and becomes void. God's speech has no nullity at its outset, unlike the speech of the lying, stubborn liar, ﴿falsehood does not come to it﴾ [Fussilat: 42], and unlike the speech of the conjecturer.

His saying: ﴿And He is the Most High, the Greatest﴾: We have already mentioned in the exegesis of His saying: ﴿That is because God is the Truth, and what they call upon besides Him is falsehood, and God is the Most High, the Greatest﴾ [al-Hajj: 62], that ﴿the Truth﴾ indicates that He is perfect, with no deficiency in Him, so He does not accept the attribution of non-existence, and is above the perfect ones, because every perfect one has above it a perfect one. So His saying ﴿the Most High, the Greatest﴾ indicates that He is above the perfect ones in His essence and His attributes. This refutes the claim that He is a body and in a place (hayyiz). For everyone who is in a place, the intellect judges that he is pointed to, and pointing comes to an end at him, because if the pointing did not reach him, the one pointed to would not be him. When pointing reaches him, pointing ends at him. At every point where pointing stops, according to the capacity of the intellect, one can imagine a greater distance, and say: If there were between the point of pointing and the one pointed to a distance greater than this, then this one pointed to would be higher, and thus would be high relatively, not absolutely. He is High in an absolute sense. And if He were a body, He would have a measure, and every measure can be imagined as greater than it, so it would be great relative to other things, not absolutely. He is Great in an absolute sense.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?﴾ We have mentioned many times that the common people worship God not because He is God, but because they seek something through Him, and that is either the averting of harm or the drawing of benefit. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: God﴾, meaning: if they do not say it, then you say it: God provides. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And indeed we or you are surely upon guidance or in manifest error﴾. And in this there are several issues:

The first issue: This is a guidance from God to His Messenger regarding the debates that take place in the sciences and other matters. This is because when one of two debaters says to the other, "What you are saying is wrong and you are mistaken in it," it angers him, and in anger the soundness of thought does not remain, and when that is disturbed there is no hope of understanding, so the aim is lost. But if he says to him, "Neither of us doubts that one of us is mistaken, and persisting in falsehood is ugly, while returning to the truth is the best of morals, so let us strive and see which of us is in error, so that he may guard against it," then that opponent will strive in consideration and abandon partisanship, and that does not entail any diminishment of rank, because he has implied that he himself is in doubt regarding his statement. This is indicated by God's words to His Prophet: ﴿And indeed we or you﴾, even though he has no doubt that he is the guide and the one guided, while they are the astray and the misleaders.

The second issue: In His words ﴿upon guidance or in manifest error﴾, He mentioned the word "upon" (ʿalā) with guidance, and the word "in" (fī) with error, because the one who is guided is as if he is elevated and looking up, so He expressed it with the particle of elevation; and the one who is astray is immersed in darkness, drowning in it, so He expressed it with the word "in."

The third issue: He described the error as "manifest" and did not describe the guidance, because guidance is the straight path that leads to the truth, while error is its opposite. But the straight path is one, and whatever is other than it is all error, and some of it is clearer than some other. So He distinguished some from others by this description.

The fourth issue: He placed guidance before error because He had described the believers mentioned with His words "we" (innā), and that comes first in mention.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind, as a bringer of good news and a warner, but most of mankind do not know.﴾

When He had explained the matter of tawhid (affirming God's oneness), He moved on to prophethood, saying: ﴿We have not sent you except comprehensively﴾. In this there are two interpretations:

The first: kāffatan means that His sending is comprehensive, that is, general to all mankind, restraining them from departing from obedience to it.

The second: kāffatan means that We sent you as one who restrains people from disbelief. On this interpretation the ha' (of kāffa, in the sense of intensive form) is for emphasis. ﴿Bashīran﴾ means that you urge them with promise, and ﴿nadhīran﴾ means that you deter them with threat. ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾: this is not because it is hidden, but because of their heedlessness.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿They say: When is this promise, if you are truthful?﴾ When He mentioned prophethood, He explained the gathering (al-hashr, the resurrection-gathering).

He said: ﴿Say: For you is an appointment of a day from which you cannot delay an hour nor advance it.﴾ We have already mentioned in Surat al-A'raf that His saying ﴿you cannot delay﴾ implies a warning, because its meaning is that there is no respite from the term. But as for "advance" (al-istiqdam), what is its aspect? We mentioned its aspect there. Here we add that when they asked for it to be hastened, He showed that there is no hastening in it, just as there is no respite. This conveys the greatness of the matter and the gravity of the affair, because a trivial matter, when someone else demands it, is not postponed or fixed to a time, unlike a weighty matter.

In God's saying ﴿For you is an appointment of a day﴾ there are readings:

First: the raising of both words with tanwin, and in this case yawmun is in apposition (badal).

Second: the accusative of yawman with the raising of mī'ād, both with tanwin, so that "mī'ādun yawman". Al-Zamakhshari said: Its aspect is that it is in the accusative governed by a verb omitted, as if he said: "an appointment, I mean a day", and this conveys glorification and awe. It may also be said that it is in the accusative as an adverbial of time, its sense being "for you is an appointment, a day", as one says: "I will come to you one day". In this case the governing element is the knowledge (al-ʿilm), as if he said: "For you is an appointment which you know, on a day", and his saying "known" (ma'lūm) indicates it, like the saying of one who says: "He will be killed one day".

Third: the idafa (genitive construction) "for you is the appointment of a day", as in the saying of one who says "suḥq thawb" (the wearing out of a garment), for explanation. The attribution of the verb to them in His saying ﴿you cannot delay from it﴾, instead of His saying "it will not be delayed from you", is an added emphasis on the occurrence of the day.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb, *The Keys to the Unseen*) on surah 34, verse 31:

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieved say, "We will never believe in this Qur'an, nor in what came before it."﴾ When He had explained the three matters, namely the Oneness of God (tawhid), prophethood (risalah), and the gathering of the dead for judgment (hashr), and they were disbelievers in all of them, He explained their general disbelief with His saying: (﴿And those who disbelieved say, "We will never believe in this Qur'an,"﴾) because the Qur'an comprises all of these. As for His saying ﴿nor in what came before it﴾, the well-known view is that it refers to the Torah and the Gospel. On this view, those who disbelieved are meant to be the polytheists who deny prophethood and the resurrection. It may also be said that the meaning is: "We do not believe that the Qur'an is from God, nor in what came before it," that is, nor in what it contains of reports, matters, verses, and proofs. On this view, those who disbelieved are meant generally, because the People of the Book did not believe that the Qur'an is from God, nor in what it contains of prophethood and the details of the gathering. If it is objected: "Do they not believe in the Oneness of God and the gathering?" we reply: when someone does not affirm the matters in the Book that are specific to it, it is said of him that he did not believe in any part of it, even if he believes in some of what it contains, because that belief is in it only insofar as it is found in other sources, so his belief is not in what is in it. An example: someone who denies a man in what he says, but when that man tells him that fire is hot, he does not deny him in this; yet it is not said that he affirmed him, because he only affirmed himself, since he already knew it beforehand. On this basis, His saying ﴿before it﴾ (bayna yadayh) means: that which it includes, insofar as it is revealed concerning it.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿If you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, returning word to one another. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Were it not for you, we would have been believers."﴾

When despair of their belief in this world had occurred through their saying "We will never believe," this was to emphasize the negation. He promised His Prophet, may blessings and peace be upon him, that He would show him them in the most humiliated state, made to stand for questioning, returning word to one another, as is the condition of a group who have erred in a matter, one saying, "This happened because of you," and the other answering him with the same. The answer to "if" (law) is omitted; its implied meaning is: "If you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand, you would see something astonishing." Then He began with the followers, because the misleader is more deserving of reproach. So He said: ﴿Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Were it not for you, we would have been believers."﴾ This indicates that their disbelief was due to an obstacle, not to a lack of the reason for belief, because they could not say, "No messenger came to us," nor say, "The messenger fell short." This points to the messenger having delivered what was upon him, for if the messenger had neglected anything, they would not have been believers. And had it not been for the arrogant, they would have believed.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed: "Did we turn you away from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals."﴾

As a response to what they said, that their disbelief was caused by an impediment: ﴿Did we turn you away from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals.﴾ The meaning is that the impediment (al-mani', the obstacle) must be stronger than the cause (al-muqtada, the motivating factor) for it to take effect. What was brought was guidance, and what came from the arrogant was not something that necessitates refusing what was brought. Therefore your attributing your disbelief to an impediment is not valid. Then He explained that their disbelief was a crime, since the one who is excused is only excused either because the cause is absent or because an impediment is present, and neither of these existed.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant: "Rather, it was the scheming of the night and the day, when you were ordering us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him."﴾

When the arrogant claimed that they had not turned us away, and that nothing that came from us was suitable to serve as an impediment or a diverting force, the oppressed acknowledged this and said: ﴿Rather, it was the scheming of the night and the day﴾ that prevented us. Then they said to them: even though you did not bring a decisive diverting force or a strong impediment, your command to us to disbelieve was joined, through the long duration and the extended period of time, to our disbelief, so we disbelieved, and thus your saying became part of the cause. It may also bear another meaning, namely that the intended meaning is "rather, your scheming by night and day," with the genitive complement omitted. As for His saying ﴿when you were ordering us to disbelieve in Allah﴾, that is, to deny Him, ﴿and set up rivals to Him﴾: this shows that the one who associates partners with Allah, although in appearance he affirms, in reality denies the existence of Allah, because whatever a created, carved thing is equated with cannot be a god. As for His saying in the first passage ﴿they will refer the speech to one another﴾, the oppressed say it using the form of the future tense (al-mustaqbal, the imperfect). In the two later verses, His saying ﴿Those who were arrogant said﴾ and ﴿And those who were oppressed said﴾ uses the past tense form (al-madi, the perfect), although the questioning and the mutual reproach in speech had not yet taken place. This is a sign that it must certainly take place, since a matter that is certain to occur is spoken of as though it has already occurred. Consider His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, you will die, and indeed they will die﴾ [az-Zumar: 30].

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment. And We will put shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they being recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾

Then they were answered and informed that there is no return for you, so they concealed that statement. As for His saying: ﴿And We will put shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved﴾, it is an indication of the manner of the punishment, and that mere seeing is not sufficient; rather, when they saw the punishment, they became certain that they were going to fall into it, so they abandoned regret and fell into it, and He placed the shackles on their necks. As for His saying: ﴿Are they being recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾, it is an indication that this is their due, by way of justice.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿We did not send a warner to any town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with."﴾ ﴿And they said, "We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished."﴾

Then he showed the flaw in their argument by His saying: ﴿It is not your wealth nor your children that will bring you near to Us in nearness, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them there is a double reward for what they did, and they will be secure in the lofty chambers.﴾

That is, your saying, "We have more wealth, so we are in a better state with God," is not a sound proof. Wealth does not bring one near to God, and no weight should be given to being strengthened by it. What is beneficial is righteous action after faith. What indicates this is that wealth and children preoccupy a person away from God and so distance him from Him; how then would they bring him near? Righteous action is turning toward God and occupying oneself with God. Whoever turns toward God arrives, and whoever asks something of God obtains it. As for His saying ﴿for them there is a double reward﴾, it means the good deed, for doubling applies only to good deeds, whereas for an evil deed only its equal is recompensed.

Then He added: ﴿and they will be secure in the lofty chambers﴾, as an indication of the permanence and perpetuity of the blessing, for one from whom blessing is cut off cannot be secure.
