Then He explained the state of the evildoer by His saying: ﴿And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them, they will be brought forth into the punishment.﴾

We have already mentioned its interpretation. His saying ﴿they will be brought forth into the punishment﴾ also indicates permanence, as the Exalted said: ﴿Whenever they wish to get out of it, they will be returned into it﴾ [al-Sajdah: 20], and as the Exalted said: ﴿And they will not be absent from it﴾ [al-Infitar: 16].

Then the Exalted said once more: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him. And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers﴾, as an indication that the bliss of the Hereafter does not contradict the blessing of this world. Rather, the righteous may receive blessings in this world, while being certain of attaining bliss in the Hereafter by virtue of the promise. This is a cut-off to the one who says: "If the immediate is ours and the deferred is theirs, then cash is better." He said: this cash is not specific to you, for many of the wretched are in poverty, and many of the pious are given enjoyment. There are issues in this:

First issue: He mentioned this meaning twice. Once to show that the abundance of their wealth and children does not indicate the goodness of their states and beliefs, and once to show that it is not specific to them, as if He said: the existence of luxury does not indicate nobility. Then even if we grant that it is so, the believers will also obtain that, for God will make them inherit your abodes and your wealth. What indicates this is that God the Exalted did not first say "for whom He wills," but said "for whom He wills," and then said "for whom He wills of His servants," and "servants" in the idafah refers to the believer. Then He promised the believer the opposite of what is for the disbelievers, for the disbeliever's last trace is cut off, his wealth is heading to decline, and his end is to ruin. As for the believer, whatever he spends God replaces, and God's replacement is better, for what is in a human's hand is exposed to ruin and loss, whereas these two cannot reach what is with God of replacement. Then He confirmed this by His saying: ﴿And God is the best of providers﴾. The excellence of a provider lies in several matters:
First: that he does not delay beyond the time of need.
Second: that he does not fall short of the measure of need.
Third: that he does not burden him with reckoning.
Fourth: that he does not trouble him by seeking reward in return.
And God the Exalted is so.

Then He explained that what they used to worship does not benefit them, saying: ﴿So today none of you will have power to benefit or harm another. And We will say to those who wronged: Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.﴾ And in this there are issues (masāʾil, points of discussion).

The first issue: To whom is the address in His words ﴿none of you﴾ directed? We say: It may be directed to the angels, because of the preceding words of His, Exalted is He: ﴿Were these the ones you used to worship?﴾ On this view, it is a rebuke (tankīl, a censure and deterrent) to the disbelievers, since it makes clear to them that what they worshipped neither benefits nor harms. This is confirmed by His words, Exalted is He: ﴿They will not have intercession, except those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful﴾ [Maryam: 87] and His words: ﴿And they will not intercede except for those whom He approves﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 28]. Also, because He said after it: ﴿And We will say to those who wronged: Taste﴾, addressing them individually. Had the addressees been the disbelievers, He would have said: "So taste."

On this view, the disbelievers are included in the address, so that the meaning of His words ﴿none of you to another﴾ is correct, that is, the angels [to the disbelievers]. A single present person may be addressed on account of someone who shares with him in a matter, just as a speaker says to one present person who has a partner in a statement: "You (plural) said it," meaning "you said it," and they said it. It may also be that the jinn are included with them, meaning: "None of you, O angels and jinn, will have power over another. And if you do not have power over them for yourselves, you will not have power over them for others." It may also be that the addressees are the disbelievers, because the mention of "today" indicates their presence. On this view, His words ﴿And We will say to those who wronged﴾ are mentioned only to emphasise the explanation of their state in wrongdoing and the cause of their punishment for sin. Had He said, "Then taste the punishment of the Fire," it would have been sufficient, but it would not achieve the benefit we have mentioned, for whenever they hear what they were upon of wrongdoing, obstinacy, sin and corruption, they will be filled with regret and remorse.

The second issue: His words ﴿benefit﴾ are relevant to regret. As for harm, what is the benefit in mentioning it, given that if they had the power to harm, that would not have benefited the disbelievers? We say: Since worship is performed to ward off the harm of the one worshipped, as a tyrant is worshipped and served out of fear of his evil, He made clear that they lack that aspect for which their worship would be fitting.

The third issue: Here He said: ﴿the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾, and in the chapter of prostration (al-Sajda) He said: ﴿the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [al-Sajda: 20]. There, He made the object of denial the punishment, and here He made the object of denial the Fire, though they used to deny everything. The benefit in this is that there, they had not seen the Fire for the first time, but had been in it for a period, as evidenced by His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Whenever they wish to get out of it, they will be returned to it, and it will be said to them: Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.﴾ That is, the lasting punishment which you denied when you said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾ [al-Baqara: 80]; that is, you said that if punishment befalls, it does not last. So taste the lasting [punishment]. Here, they are seeing the Fire for the first time, because it is mentioned following the gathering (ḥashr) and the questioning (suʾāl). So it is said to them: "This is the Fire which you used to deny."

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, "This is none but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship." And they say, "This is none but a fabricated lie." And those who disbelieve say of the truth when it comes to them, "This is none but obvious magic."﴾

(This is) to demonstrate the corruption of their belief and the intensity of their obstinacy, since it becomes clear that the highest of those they worship, namely the angels, are not qualified for worship in their own right, as they said: ﴿Glory be to You; You are our Guardian, not them﴾ [Saba: 41]. That is, we have no fitness except to worship You rather than them; that is, we have no fitness to be worshipped by them, nor to benefit or harm. As the Exalted said: ﴿So on that Day none of you will possess for another any benefit or harm﴾. Then, despite all this, when the Prophet ﷺ spoke to them words of tawhid (monotheism) and recited to them the verses of Allah that indicate it, (for indeed, in everything there are signs of Allah indicating His oneness), they denied them and said: "This is none but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship." That is, they oppose the proof with blind imitation (taqlid). ﴿And they say, "This is none but a fabricated lie."﴾ This has several possible meanings:

First: that the intended meaning is that the statement of monotheism is ﴿a fabricated lie﴾. This is supported by the fact that the monotheist used to say about the polytheist that he is "deluded" (ya'fik), as the Exalted said about them: ﴿Do you want falsehoods, gods other than Allah?﴾ [al-Saffat: 86], and as they themselves said to the Messenger: ﴿Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods?﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 22].

Second: that the intended meaning is "This is none but a lie," that is, the Qur'an is a lie. According to the first meaning, His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say of the truth when it comes to them, "This is none but obvious magic."﴾ [Saba: 43] refers to the Qur'an, and according to the second it refers to the miracles he brought. On both interpretations, the Exalted's saying ﴿And those who disbelieve﴾ instead of saying "and they said of the truth" indicates that the denial of monotheism was specific to the polytheists, whereas the denial of the Qur'an and the miracles was agreed upon among the polytheists and the People of the Book. Therefore the Exalted said ﴿And those who disbelieve say of the truth﴾ in a general sense.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿We did not give them any books that they could study, nor did We send to them, before you, any warner.﴾

That is, when the clear verses are recited to them, they say, "This is a lying man," and their saying is: ﴿a fabricated lie﴾, without any proof, without a book revealed to them, and without a messenger sent to them. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: I admonish you with one thing: that you stand up for Allah in pairs and singly, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion; he is only a warner to you before a severe punishment.﴾

In this verse He mentioned the three foundations (al-usul al-thalathah) after He had established them with proofs. So His saying ﴿that you stand up for Allah﴾ is an indication of tawhid (oneness of God), His saying ﴿there is no madness in your companion; he is only a warner to you﴾ is an indication of prophethood (al-risalah), and His saying ﴿before a severe punishment﴾ is an indication of the Last Day. In the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: His saying ﴿I admonish you with one thing﴾ implies that there is nothing except tawhid, yet faith is not complete except by acknowledging prophethood and resurrection. So how is the restriction stated in His saying ﴿I admonish you with one thing﴾ valid? We say: tawhid is the aim, and whoever affirms the oneness of Allah with true affirmation, Allah expands his breast and raises his rank in the Hereafter. So the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded them with what opens for them the doors of worship and prepares for them the causes of happiness. Another answer is that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not say, "I will not command you during all my life except with one thing," but rather he said, "I admonish you first with tawhid, and I do not command you at the beginning of the matter with anything else," because it precedes everything. This is indicated by His saying ﴿then reflect﴾, for reflection too has become something commanded and admonished.

It is possible to say that the intended meaning is one good deed (hasanah wahidah), because tawhid is a good deed and a beautiful act (ihsan). We have mentioned in His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah commands justice and ihsan﴾ [al-Nahl: 90] that justice (al-'adl) is the negation of divinity from other than Allah, and ihsan is the affirmation of divinity for Him. It has been said in the interpretation of His saying ﴿Is the reward of ihsan anything but ihsan?﴾ [al-Rahman: 60] that the intended meaning is: is the reward of faith anything but paradise (al-jinan)? Likewise, this is indicated by His saying ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah﴾ [Fussilat: 33].

The third issue: His saying ﴿in pairs and singly﴾ indicates all states, for a person is either with another or alone. If he is with another, he is included in His saying ﴿in pairs﴾, and if he is alone, he is included in His saying ﴿singly﴾. It is as if He is saying: stand up for Allah gathered together and alone, neither togetherness prevents you from remembering Allah, nor does solitude make you need a helper who assists you in remembering Allah.

This is because the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to display things that are not within human capacity, and those from whom wonders appear other than humans are either jinn or angels. If what came from the Prophet (ﷺ) was not through the mediation of jinn, then it was through the mediation of an angel or by the power of Allah the Exalted without any intermediary. When they agreed to that, the matter became binding upon them. This is why He said after it: ﴿he is only a warner﴾, meaning: either he has madness, or he is a messenger; but it has become clear that he has no madness, so he is a warner.

The sixth issue: His saying ﴿before a severe punishment﴾ indicates the nearness of the punishment, as if He said: he warns you of a punishment that is present, which will touch you soon. "Before the punishment" means that the punishment will come after it.

Then God Most High said: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours. My reward is only from God, and He is Witness over all things.﴾

When He mentioned that there was no madness in him, which would necessitate his being a prophet, He mentioned another aspect which necessitates that he is a prophet if he is not insane. The Prophet ﷺ, by his claim to prophethood, makes himself liable to swift destruction, for everyone opposes him and is hostile to him. Someone who does not seek worldly reward does what he does for the sake of the Hereafter, and the liar in the Hereafter is punished, not rewarded. So if he were a liar he would be insane, but he is not insane, therefore he is not a liar; he is a truthful prophet. His saying ﴿and He is Witness over all things﴾ is another affirmation of the message, because prophethood is established only by a claim and a proof: a person claims prophethood and God displays a miracle for him, which is a witnessing proof, and confirmation by action stands in the place of confirmation by words in conveying knowledge. The evidence is that whoever says to a people, "I am sent to you by this king," obliges them to accept his word, while the king is present and watching. Then he says to the king, "O king, if I am truly your messenger to them, then tell them that I am your messenger." When he says that he is my messenger to you, no doubt remains. Likewise, if he says, "O king, if I am truly your messenger to them, then clothe me in your robe," and the king clothes him in his robe immediately after his words, people will be certain that he is his messenger. Similarly is the case of the messengers: when the prophets say to their people, "We are messengers of God," and then say, "O our God, if we are Your messengers, then make these stones speak or raise this dead man," and He does it, certainty is attained that He confirmed them.

Then God Most High said: ﴿Say: Indeed my Lord hurls the truth; the Knower of the unseen.﴾ In this there are two aspects:

The first: He hurls the truth into the hearts of those who seek the truth. On this view the verse is connected to what precedes it, in that when God Most High explained the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ with His saying ﴿He is only a warner to you﴾ [Saba': 46], and affirmed it with His saying ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours,﴾ and it was the custom of the polytheists to find it improbable that one among them should be singled out for the revelation of the Reminder, as God said of them: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us?﴾ [Sad: 8], He mentioned what would serve as an answer to them, saying: ﴿Say: Indeed my Lord hurls the truth,﴾ that is, into the hearts, indicating that the matter is in His hand: He does what He wills and gives what He wills to whom He wills.

* * *

Then God Most High said: ﴿the Knower of the unseen﴾, as an indication of the answer to a flawed objection that may be raised, namely that one who does something as he wills, without the place of the action being specially determined by something not found elsewhere, is not knowing, and that he did it by chance, as when an arrow strikes one spot rather than another although the spots are equal in their facing. So He said: ﴿hurls the truth﴾ as He wills, and He is knowing of what He does and knowing of the consequences of what He does. He does what He wills, not as the heedless assailant does, unmindful of consequences, since He is the Knower of the unseen.

The second aspect: the meaning is that He hurls the truth against falsehood, as He said in Surah al-Anbiya': ﴿Nay, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it﴾ [al-Anbiya': 18]. On this aspect too the connection with what precedes is evident, in that when the proofs of monotheism appeared and refuted their doubts, He said: ﴿Say: Indeed my Lord hurls the truth,﴾ that is, against your falsehood. And His saying ﴿the Knower of the unseen﴾ on this aspect has a subtle meaning: the clear rational proof manifested itself only for monotheism and prophethood, whereas for the Gathering, its occurrence has no proof other than God's report about it and about its states and terrors, and had God not explained it by speech, it would not have become clear to anyone, unlike monotheism and prophethood. So when He said ﴿hurls the truth﴾, that is, against falsehood, indicating the manifestation of the proofs for monotheism and prophethood, He said ﴿the Knower of the unseen﴾, that is, what He informs of the unseen, namely the Hour and its conditions, so there is no doubt about it, for God is the Knower of the unseen. ﴿Say: Indeed my Lord hurls the truth; the Knower of the unseen.﴾

* * *

* * *

Then God Most High said: ﴿the Knower of the unseen﴾, as an indication of the answer to a flawed objection that may be raised, namely that one who does something as he wills, without the place of the action being specially determined by something not found elsewhere, is not knowing, and that he did it by chance, as when an arrow strikes one spot rather than another although the spots are equal in their facing. So when He said ﴿hurls the truth﴾, that is, against falsehood, indicating the manifestation of the proofs for monotheism and prophethood, He said ﴿the Knower of the unseen﴾, that is, what He informs of the unseen, namely the Hour and its conditions, so there is no doubt about it, for God is the Knower of the unseen. The first: It is the Qur'an.

The second: It is the explanation of tawhid (Oneness of God), resurrection (hashr), and everything that appeared upon the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ.

The third: The miracles that indicate the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). And since what they bring, such as shirk and denial, cannot exist, it is falsehood that does not establish itself. [صفحة ٢٣٥]

* * *

Then God the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "If I stray, I only stray to my own detriment; and if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me. Indeed He is Hearing, Near."﴾ This also affirms the prophethood, because God the Exalted said in general terms: ﴿Whoever is guided, it is for his own self﴾ [al-Zumar: 41], and He said concerning the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿and if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me.﴾ That is, "my straying is to my own detriment, just as your straying is to yours. As for my guidance, it is not by reflection and inference as your guidance is, but by clear revelation." His saying ﴿Indeed He is Hearing﴾ means: He hears when I call upon Him and seek His help against you. ﴿Near﴾ means: He comes to you without delay. He does not hear from a distance, nor does He fail to reach the one who calls upon Him.

* * *

Then God the Exalted said: ﴿If only you could see when they are seized with terror, with no escape, and they are seized from a near place.﴾

When He said ﴿Hearing﴾, He said ﴿Near﴾. So if He does not punish swiftly, and does not immediately help the one who has the right, then the Day of terror is coming, and there is no escape. Only one who fears missing out hastens. His saying ﴿If only you could see﴾ has an omitted response, meaning: "you would see a marvel." ﴿And they are seized from a near place﴾ means they cannot flee, since the seizing occurs before they are able to escape.

* * *

Then God the Exalted said: ﴿And they will say, "We believe in it." But how can they reach [it] from a distant place?﴾

That is, after the matter has become evident, when faith no longer benefits, they will say, "We believe." ﴿But how can they reach [it]﴾: that is, how can they manage to attain the desired goal? That is not possible except in this world, while they are in the Hereafter. And the world is far from the Hereafter. If it is said: "How then has He said in many places that the Hereafter is near to this world, and that is why God named it the Hour, and said: ﴿It may be that the Hour is near﴾ [al-Shura: 17]?" We say: the past is like yesterday that has gone, since there is no way to reach it. The future, even if there are years between it and the present, is still coming. So on the Day of Resurrection the world is far, because it has passed, while in the world the Day of Resurrection is near, because it is coming. And "tanawush" (reaching out and grasping) means taking hold from near. It is also said to mean from far. Since God made the action like a body that is grasped, He made the container of the action, which is time, like the container of the body, which is place, and so He said ﴿from a distant place﴾. What is meant is what has passed of the world.

Then God explained that their faith is of no benefit, because they disbelieved in it before. The reference in His saying ﴿We believe in it﴾ and His saying ﴿and they had disbelieved in it before﴾ is to one and the same thing: either Muhammad (ﷺ), or the Qur'an, or the truth that Muhammad (ﷺ) brought. The last is closer and more appropriate. As for the disbeliever, he hurls [guesses] at the unseen, meaning he says what he does not know. His saying ﴿from a distant place﴾ may mean that their source is far: they took a partner [for God] from the fact that they cannot perform many actions unless they are many persons, and so created beings are also many. And they took [an analogy] after the resurrection from their own condition and their inability to give life, for a sick person is treated, but once he dies it is not possible for them to restore the soul to him; and analogizing God to created beings is a far-fetched source. It may also be said that they used to say that when the Hour is established, reward and bliss will be ours, like the saying of one of them: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have with Him the best [reward].﴾ So they used to say that. If it was from the saying of the Messenger, then it was not [known] to them, so that they would say it on the basis of perception. What is not necessary by reason is known only through perception or through the word of the truthful one. So they were speaking about the unseen from a distant place.

[صفحة ٢٣٦]

First: that [Hereafter] is near for one who believes in Muhammad (ﷺ), but one who does not believe cannot confirm it, so it is distant for him.

And this is a hurling of [guesses] at the unseen from a distant place, which is the world.

﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, as was done with their counterparts before; indeed they were in disquieting doubt.﴾

* * *

Then God the Exalted said: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾, namely the return to the world, or between them and the pleasures of the world. If it is asked: "How is your statement correct that [it is] what they desire of returning, when He said: ﴿as was done with their counterparts before; indeed they were in disquieting doubt﴾, and no barrier was placed between them and the return?" We say: Why do you say that no barrier was placed between them? Rather, everyone to whom the angel came asked for a delay and was not given it; and they wished to believe at the moment hopelessness appeared, but it was not accepted. His saying ﴿disquieting [mureeb]﴾ may have two meanings:

One: possessing doubt.

The second: causing doubt.

We will mention it in another place, God willing. And God knows best what is right. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and His blessings be upon the best of His creation, Muhammad the Prophet, and upon his family, his companions, and all his wives.

What is meant is what has passed of the world.

He does not hear from a distance, nor does He fail to reach the one who calls upon Him.
